title: Mitigate SSE mid-stream encoding mismatches causing truncated/garbled partial outputs
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Multiple customers reported that long-lived Server-Sent Events (SSE) responses sometimes terminate with truncated or corrupted partial outputs. Root symptoms included invalid UTF-8 sequences in streamed text, unexpected duplicate fragments, and clients treating mid-stream transport disconnects as final EOF. This ticket captures investigation and remediation for encoding/fragment loss during reconnects.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a hosted SSE session with a model that streams multi-kilobyte responses (e.g., long summarization).
2) Simulate an intermittent network blip by dropping TCP for 1-3 seconds on the client side.
3) Reconnect using the same client that attempts to resume the stream without a server-side resume token.
4) Observe the client concatenating the last partial chunk with the new stream leading to malformed UTF-8 or duplicated phrases.
investigation: 2026-03-05 - Initial triage: Customer A (enterprise) produced crash logs showing invalid UTF-8 on final response; observed by SDK telemetry.
2026-03-06 - Captured packet traces from customer environment to reproduce; saw chunk boundary splits mid-codepoint across TCP segments.
2026-03-07 - Reproduced locally with fast network flapping; server-side logs show chunks emitted without checksum or boundary guarantees, and reconnects create overlapping partials.
2026-03-08 - Reviewed runtime's streaming buffer: it emits deltas immediately; no chunk-level metadata beyond SSE 'data:' lines. Resume handshake lacks an explicit offset/sequence id.
2026-03-09 - Confirmed existing resume behavior relies on client dedup heuristics; clients do not always detect mid-codepoint splits, causing garbled decoding.
impact: Multiple paid customers seeing corrupted streamed outputs in production. High-impact for chat/streaming UIs where partial outputs are shown incrementally. Several escalations opened with support; some customers temporarily disabled streaming to avoid UX regressions.
root_cause: Lack of chunk-level integrity metadata and a resume protocol leads to ambiguous reconstruction after a disconnect. Payloads may be split mid-UTF-8 codepoint across network retransmits; clients resume naive concatenation, producing invalid text. No server-side durable resume tokens or chunk checksums were present.
proposed_fix: A) Add per-chunk sequence IDs and length headers in the SSE 'data' payload (backwards-compatible framing): e.g., data: {"seq":123,"len":512,"crc":"abcd"}\n
B) Emit a final 'chunk_end' marker for each logical delta and ensure server never splits a UTF-8 codepoint across emitted chunk boundaries.
C) Implement a resume handshake where client provides last-seen seq and server replays from seq+1 or returns a snapshot if gap too large.
D) Add CRC32 checksum on each chunk to allow clients to detect corruption and request replay.
E) Short-term mitigation: disable immediate emission of partial byte ranges for large tokens—buffer to codepoint boundary.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Implement framing and checksum in server runtime behind a feature flag; ship SDK patch that understands new framing and falls back to original behavior. Deploy to a small set of hosted nodes (1 AZ) and opt-in customers.
Phase 2 (Wider rollout): Enable feature for all hosted streams, keep legacy fallback for very old SDKs for 30 days; monitor errors and UX regressions.
Phase 3 (Enforcement): After 30 days and telemetry threshold met, remove legacy fallback and require framing for resume flows; publish migration notes.
Rollback: Feature flag can be disabled quickly; SDK maintains acceptance of legacy plain-data SSE to avoid hard breaks during rollback.
qa_criteria: Automated unit tests validating chunk framing, sequence increment, and CRC mismatch detection.
Integration test simulating network blips and reconnection with exact byte-split scenarios.
End-to-end tests with web SDK and mobile SDK showing no UTF-8 corruption across reconnects.
Load test to ensure the additional headers and buffering do not increase P99 latency beyond SLA.
Customer acceptance test with Customer A verifying streaming stability on their environment.

2026-03-06: Reproduced locally; started a small spike to prototype framing.
2026-03-07: Prototype framing accepted by runtime owners; CRC library chosen (crc32c).

notes: Security: framing does not include sensitive data; adding CRC is safe. Will add security_review_required flag for on-prem/private deployments where KMS restrictions apply.
Telemetry: create new metric 'sse.replay_requests' and 'sse.crc_mismatch' to measure effectiveness.
Customer communication: Draft email template to notify customers of upcoming opt-in canary and migration timeline.
